- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot early in the 30-day horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over recent days; model fails to account for downward momentum.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to recent volatility, then incorrectly assumes price will return to “normal” too quickly.
- When sentiment turns sharply negative, model delays correction — prices drop faster than forecasted.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing sentiment-driven reversals; model often misses early signs of sentiment-driven corrections.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., +1.09 sentiment) — model assumes momentum continues longer than it does.
- When sentiment is mixed or trending sideways, model tends to average out, underestimating volatility and overestimating stability.
- Model underestimates downward pressure in late horizon (e.g., days 20–30) when sentiment is negative — often fails to recognize “selloff” triggers.
